classification: The failing48k Hann maximum is overwhelmingly an already-present modeled pre-decimator baseband component. Output FIR folding/roundoff and low H1-H3 Hann leakage do not account for it. A contact-noise control diagnostic reduces its maximum substantially. This does not certify physical harmonic/noise correctness, exclude every upstream nonlinear/numerical artifact, invalidate the unchanged guard, or approve the product candidate.
limits: No production patch, guard alteration, floor lowering, reclassification of prior frozen result or real-guitar render.
Double FIR is diagnostic, not a proposed precision/filter change; exact native PCM retained.
A finite-window folding channel can itself contain spectral leakage; neither frequency>12k nor rate change alone proves an alias defect.
Low-partial nuisance is an estimated lower-bound comparator, not a calibrated source or complete low-band physical decomposition.
Different internal rates change sample-clock interpolation, stochastic forcing and other numerical trajectories despite fixed static controls.
No audible defect or invalid-contract conclusion follows from these extremely quiet absolute levels alone.

Hann fold/image estimate at the failing bin is near double cancellation scale; do not report its ~-301dBFS estimate as resolved signal. Identity residual is about1e-15 absolute, still negligible relative to~3.6e-9 native amplitude.
Incidental-path public-control zeroing is a nonlinear diagnostic, not an independent additive noise stem or variance subtraction.

H1-H3/all-under1k reconstructions do not isolate every possible1-12k leakage contribution. BH supports surviving upper energy but has its own endpoint leakage, particularly near quiet baseline levels.
The original48k guard still fails; no guard, source pin, threshold, floor, coefficient, gain, productdefault or real-reference admission has changed.
No Longitudinal/SG reference renders were made in this diagnostic. Root decides any subsequent research-only comparison separately.
